newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernogorneft plans 2 pct output rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chernogorneft plans 2 pct output rise in 1997.

text.p: Russian oil company AOOT Chernogorneft plans to increase oil output by two percent in 1997 from a planned 43.67 million barrels this year, a company official said on Thursday.
Boris Korolyov, head of investor relations, told Reuters the plan had been agreed at a board meeting on November 5, but it depended on the company raising financing of at least $45 million.
This could be done by raising a long-term foreign credit, or by issuing shares, he said.

Company figures show that 1996 output is running below plan. In the first three quarters of this year output was 30.37 million barrels, implying a total for the year of 40.49 million. Actual output in 1995 was 44.45 million barrels.
